title: King Baudouin Temporarily Removed Over Abortion Law Refusal
description: King Baudouin refused to sign the law decriminalizing abortion on grounds of Catholic conscience, prompting the government to invoke a constitutional mechanism declaring him temporarily unable to reign. Parliament enacted the law in his absence and restored his powers 36 hours later, creating a unique constitutional precedent.

title: Black Sunday Election Breakthrough for Vlaams Blok
description: The far-right Vlaams Blok made dramatic gains in the November 1991 federal elections, winning 12 seats in the Chamber and shocking the political establishment. The results, dubbed Black Sunday, prompted all mainstream parties to formalize a cordon sanitaire excluding the party from any coalition.

title: Maastricht Treaty Signed with Belgium as EU Founding Member
description: Belgium signed the Maastricht Treaty establishing the European Union and laying the groundwork for economic and monetary union. As host of EU institutions in Brussels, Belgium's role as the de facto capital of the emerging Union was further cemented.

title: Saint-Michel Agreement Restructures Belgian Federalism
description: The Saint-Michel Agreement of September 1992 laid the groundwork for transforming Belgium into a fully federal state by devolving powers to the Communities and Regions. The accord resolved a prolonged linguistic community crisis triggered by disputes over arms sales and economic policy between Flemish and Walloon parties.

title: Belgium Formally Becomes a Federal State
description: Parliament approved constitutional amendments in July 1993 transforming Belgium from a unitary into a federal state, with Article 1 now reading: Belgium is a Federal State which consists of communities and regions. The reform completed the devolution process begun in 1970 and gave Communities and Regions full autonomous powers.

title: Death of King Baudouin After 42-Year Reign
description: King Baudouin died of a heart attack on 31 July 1993 while on holiday in Spain, ending a 42-year reign that had seen Belgium's transformation from a colonial power to a federal state. His brother Albert II succeeded to the throne amid an outpouring of national mourning that temporarily bridged linguistic divides.

title: Ten Belgian Peacekeepers Killed in Rwanda Genocide
description: On 7 April 1994, ten Belgian UNAMIR paratroopers were murdered by Rwandan government soldiers in Kigali while guarding Prime Minister Agathe Uwilingiyimana. Belgium withdrew its contingent in response, effectively crippling the UN peacekeeping mission. The killings deeply traumatized Belgium and triggered lasting debate over the country's colonial legacy in the Great Lakes region.

title: Province of Brabant Split Along Linguistic Lines
description: Following the 1993 constitutional reform, the bilingual province of Brabant was formally divided into Flemish Brabant and Walloon Brabant on 1 January 1995, with the Brussels-Capital Region becoming a separate entity. The split was a concrete manifestation of Belgium's deepening federal fragmentation along the linguistic boundary.

title: Dutroux Affair Exposed Systemic Police and Judicial Failures
description: Marc Dutroux was arrested on 13 August 1996, and police found kidnapped girls Sabine Dardenne and Laetitia Delhez alive in his basement, while four other victims were found dead. The subsequent investigation revealed catastrophic failures in police coordination and judicial oversight, destroying public trust in Belgian institutions.

title: White March Draws 300,000 Protesters to Brussels
description: On 20 October 1996, approximately 300,000 people marched through Brussels demanding reform of the justice system and better child protection in the wake of the Dutroux affair. The White March was one of the largest demonstrations in Belgian history, representing roughly three percent of the national population and uniting both linguistic communities in rare solidarity.

title: Dutroux Escape Triggers Government Minister Resignations
description: Marc Dutroux briefly escaped custody on 23 April 1998 by overpowering a guard at the Neufchateau courthouse, triggering the immediate resignations of Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck and Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte. The incident deepened the crisis of confidence in Belgian institutions and accelerated police reform.

title: Dioxin Food Contamination Scandal Topples Government
description: A dioxin contamination discovered in Belgian poultry feed in early 1999 led to a massive food safety crisis affecting eggs, chicken, and pork products across the EU. The scandal, which exposed regulatory failures, contributed directly to the historic defeat of Jean-Luc Dehaene's Christian Democratic coalition in the June 1999 elections.

title: Verhofstadt Forms First Purple Coalition Without Christian Democrats
description: Guy Verhofstadt became prime minister at the head of a purple coalition comprising liberals, socialists, and greens, marking the first Belgian government without a Christian Democratic party since 1958. The coalition's formation ended four decades of unbroken Christian Democratic participation in government and signaled a generational political realignment.

title: Sabena Airlines Collapses Into Bankruptcy
description: Belgium's national carrier Sabena filed for legal protection on 3 October 2001 and entered liquidation on 6 November after partner Swissair failed to inject promised capital. The bankruptcy, compounded by the post-September 11 aviation crisis, left over 12,000 employees jobless and ended 78 years of Belgian flag-carrier aviation.

title: Belgium Formally Apologizes for Lumumba Assassination Role
description: Prime Minister Guy Verhofstadt officially apologized on behalf of Belgium for the country's involvement in the 1961 assassination of Congo's first prime minister Patrice Lumumba. Foreign Minister Louis Michel read a statement acknowledging moral responsibility to the Lumumba, Mpolo, and Okito families, marking Belgium's first formal reckoning with its colonial violence.

title: Belgium Hosts NATO-EU Berlin Plus Agreement
description: NATO and the European Union signed the Berlin Plus arrangement on 16 December 2002 at NATO headquarters in Brussels, giving the EU access to NATO planning capabilities for independent crisis management operations. The agreement formalized the institutional relationship between the two organizations both headquartered in the Belgian capital.

title: Nuclear Phase-Out Law Enacted Banning New Reactors
description: Belgium's federal parliament passed the law of 31 January 2003 prohibiting the construction of new nuclear power plants and limiting existing reactors to 40-year operating lifetimes. The law set a phased closure schedule with all seven reactors to be shut down by 2025, making Belgium one of the first European countries to legislate a complete nuclear exit.

title: Belgium Legalizes Euthanasia Among First Countries Worldwide
description: Belgium became one of the first countries in the world to legalize euthanasia under strict medical conditions with the law of 28 May 2002 taking effect in September 2002, and further expanded in 2014 to include terminally ill minors. The legislation positioned Belgium at the forefront of end-of-life rights debates in Europe.

title: Vlaams Blok Convicted of Racism and Forced to Dissolve
description: The Ghent Court of Appeal ruled in April 2004 that organizations affiliated with the far-right Vlaams Blok had breached Belgium's 1981 anti-racism law by systematically inciting discrimination. The party dissolved and immediately reconstituted as Vlaams Belang, but the conviction reinforced the cordon sanitaire and demonstrated Belgium's judicial approach to far-right extremism.

title: Federal Elections Trigger Prolonged Government Formation Crisis
description: The June 2007 federal elections produced a fragmented result with Yves Leterme's CD&V/N-VA cartel winning the most Flemish votes but unable to form a government due to Flemish demands for further state reform. Negotiations dragged on for 194 days, requiring interim Prime Minister Verhofstadt to serve as caretaker, foreshadowing the even longer deadlock of 2010-2011.

title: Fortis Bank Nationalization During Global Financial Crisis
description: Fortis, Belgium's largest financial institution, was partially nationalized on 28 September 2008 after its over-leveraged acquisition of ABN Amro left it unable to weather the global credit crunch. Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg injected 11.2 billion euros, and the Belgian operations were subsequently sold to BNP Paribas in a controversial deal that prompted shareholder lawsuits.

title: Dexia Bank Requires Emergency Bailout
description: Franco-Belgian bank Dexia received a 6.4 billion euro emergency capital injection from the Belgian, French, and Luxembourg governments in September 2008 after toxic asset exposure threatened its collapse. Dexia would require a second bailout in 2011 and eventual dismantling, costing Belgian taxpayers billions and exposing the risks of municipal finance speculation.

title: Federal Elections Begin Record 541-Day Government Deadlock
description: The 13 June 2010 elections produced irreconcilable results with the Flemish nationalist N-VA under Bart De Wever winning 27 seats and the Francophone Socialist Party winning 26. The split between Flemish demands for confederalism and Francophone resistance to further devolution made coalition formation impossible for 541 days, a world record for a democracy without a government.

title: Di Rupo Sworn In After World-Record Government Formation
description: Elio Di Rupo was sworn in as prime minister on 6 December 2011 after 541 days of negotiations, ending the longest government formation in modern democratic history. His six-party coalition excluded the N-VA and made Di Rupo Belgium's first Francophone socialist prime minister since the 1970s and the first openly gay head of government in the world.

title: General Strike Against Austerity Pension Reforms
description: Belgian public sector unions called a general strike on 22 December 2011 against the Di Rupo government's austerity package, which aimed to achieve 11.3 billion euros in savings including pension age increases. The strike paralyzed public transport, schools, and government services, reflecting widespread opposition to EU-mandated fiscal consolidation.

title: BHV Electoral District Split Resolves Decades-Old Dispute
description: The Chamber of Representatives voted on 13 July 2012 to split the Brussels-Halle-Vilvoorde electoral district, resolving a dispute that had paralyzed Belgian politics since 2007. The split separated Flemish Brabant's Halle-Vilvoorde area from the Brussels-Capital Region for electoral purposes, eliminating the anomaly that allowed Francophone candidates to campaign in Flemish territory.

title: Sixth State Reform Devolves 20 Billion Euros in Powers
description: The Butterfly Agreement, named after Di Rupo's trademark bow tie, launched Belgium's sixth state reform transferring approximately 20 billion euros in annual competencies from the federal level to the Regions and Communities. The reform devolved employment policy, family allowances, and substantial fiscal autonomy, representing the largest power transfer in Belgian federal history.

title: Charles Michel Forms Centre-Right Coalition with N-VA
description: Charles Michel was sworn in on 11 October 2014 as the youngest Belgian prime minister since 1841, leading a centre-right coalition of MR, N-VA, Open Vld, and CD&V. The inclusion of the Flemish nationalist N-VA in a federal government for the first time marked a significant political shift and sidelined all Francophone parties except Michel's own MR.

title: NATO Wales Summit Increases Belgian Defense Commitments
description: At the NATO summit in Wales, Belgium joined allies in pledging to move toward spending two percent of GDP on defense within a decade, up from approximately one percent. Belgium's hosting of NATO headquarters in Evere, Brussels, underscored the disconnect between its central role in the alliance and its consistently low defense spending.

title: Molenbeek Linked to Paris Attacks Sparks Security Overhaul
description: The November 2015 Paris attacks that killed 130 people were traced to a jihadist cell operating from the Brussels commune of Molenbeek, exposing critical gaps in Belgian intelligence coordination. Belgium raised its terror threat to the maximum level and locked down Brussels for days while police hunted suspects, triggering a national debate over radicalization and security failures.

title: Brussels Airport and Metro Bombings Kill 32 People
description: On 22 March 2016, ISIS-linked suicide bombers struck Brussels Airport at Zaventem and the Maalbeek metro station in the EU quarter, killing 32 people and injuring over 300. The attackers belonged to the same cell responsible for the November 2015 Paris attacks, and the bombings exposed Belgium's fragmented security architecture across 19 Brussels communes and six police zones.

title: N-VA Exits Government Over UN Migration Pact Dispute
description: The New Flemish Alliance withdrew from the governing coalition in December 2018 over Prime Minister Michel's decision to sign the UN Global Compact for Migration in Marrakech. Michel continued briefly with a minority government but resigned on 18 December after parliament passed a motion of no confidence, triggering early elections in May 2019.

title: Youth Climate Strikes Mobilize Tens of Thousands Weekly
description: Inspired by Greta Thunberg, Belgian students led by Anuna De Wever and Adelaida Charlier organized weekly school strikes from January 2019 that drew up to 35,000 marchers in Brussels. The movement dominated the political agenda ahead of the May 2019 elections and contributed to the resignation of Flemish Environment Minister Joke Schauvliege, who falsely claimed the protests were orchestrated by intelligence services.

title: Fragmented Elections Produce Record Vlaams Belang Gains
description: The 26 May 2019 federal elections produced extreme fragmentation with N-VA and Vlaams Belang together winning over 43 percent of the Flemish vote, while Francophone socialists and greens gained in Wallonia. Vlaams Belang tripled its seats from 3 to 18, its best federal result ever, making coalition formation across the linguistic divide extremely difficult.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Devastates Belgian Care Homes
description: Belgium suffered one of the highest per-capita COVID-19 death rates in the EU, with over half of deaths occurring in care homes for the elderly. Prime Minister Sophie Wilmes, who had been leading a minority caretaker government, was granted emergency powers and defended Belgium's transparent but unflattering counting methodology that included suspected as well as confirmed deaths.

title: De Croo Vivaldi Coalition Formed After 493-Day Negotiations
description: Alexander De Croo was sworn in as prime minister on 1 October 2020 at the head of a seven-party Vivaldi coalition comprising liberals, socialists, greens, and CD&V. The 493-day formation period was the second longest in Belgian history, and the coalition explicitly excluded all Flemish nationalist parties.

title: King Philippe Expresses Regrets for Colonial Past in Congo
description: On the 60th anniversary of Congolese independence on 30 June 2020, King Philippe sent a letter to President Tshisekedi expressing his deepest regrets for the suffering and humiliation inflicted during Belgian colonial rule. While falling short of a formal apology, the letter was unprecedented in Belgian royal history and reflected growing domestic pressure for colonial reckoning.

title: Catastrophic Floods Kill 39 in Wallonia
description: Unprecedented rainfall between 12-15 July 2021 caused the Vesdre, Ourthe, Ambleve, and Meuse rivers to burst their banks, killing 39 people and causing an estimated 2.8 billion euros in damage across Wallonia. The disaster was Belgium's deadliest natural event in decades and intensified the national debate over climate adaptation infrastructure.

title: Lumumba's Remains Returned to Congo in Colonial Reckoning
description: Belgium returned a gold-crowned tooth believed to be the last physical remains of Patrice Lumumba to his family in a ceremony at the Egmont Palace in Brussels on 20 June 2022. The tooth had been seized by a Belgian police commissioner who participated in the dissolution of Lumumba's body in acid after his 1961 assassination.

title: Colonial Reckoning Commission Fails to Approve Formal Apology
description: Belgium's parliamentary commission investigating the colonial past announced in late 2022 that it could not approve a formal apology to victims of colonialism in Congo, Rwanda, and Burundi, despite two years of hearings with nearly 300 witnesses. Liberal parties blocked the apology over fears it would trigger financial reparations claims, drawing criticism from civil society organizations.

title: Belgium Extends Two Nuclear Reactors Amid Energy Crisis
description: Amid the European energy crisis triggered by the Russia-Ukraine war, Prime Minister De Croo announced in March 2022 that Belgium would extend the operation of the Doel 4 and Tihange 3 nuclear reactors by ten years beyond their planned 2025 closure. The reversal marked a significant retreat from the 2003 nuclear phase-out law under pressure from energy security concerns.

title: Federal Elections Confirm Rightward Shift in Flanders
description: The 9 June 2024 federal, regional, and European elections saw Vlaams Belang win nearly one million votes and become the largest party in three of five Flemish provinces, while N-VA maintained its position as Belgium's largest party overall. The results confirmed a structural rightward shift in Flanders and set the stage for the most complex coalition negotiations in Belgian history.

title: Bart De Wever Becomes First Flemish Nationalist Prime Minister
description: N-VA leader Bart De Wever was sworn in as prime minister on 3 February 2025 at the head of the five-party Arizona coalition comprising N-VA, CD&V, Vooruit, MR, and Les Engages. The appointment of Belgium's first Flemish nationalist prime minister marked a historic shift after nearly eight months of difficult negotiations following the June 2024 elections.

title: Belgium Reverses Nuclear Phase-Out With New Expansion Law
description: The Belgian parliament voted 102 to 8 on 15 May 2025 to repeal the 2003 nuclear phase-out law, enabling both the continued operation of existing reactors and the construction of new nuclear capacity. Energy Minister Mathieu Bihet announced plans to double nuclear capacity from 4 to 8 gigawatts, marking a dramatic reversal of two decades of energy policy.

title: Materialise Founded in Belgium, Pioneering Industrial 3D Printing in Europe
description: Wilfried Vancraen and Hilde Ingelaere founded Materialise in Leuven, Belgium in June 1990 after acquiring one of the first stereolithography 3D-printing machines in Europe, making it the first company of its kind in the Benelux region. In 1992 Materialise began digitally mapping human anatomy from CT scan data, developing its Mimics medical image-processing software and helping establish 3D printing as an industrial technology in Europe.
